script.title: Why Three Stars Can Never Truly Stay Together
script.description: A silent numerical simulation illustrates how chaotic energy transfers inevitably resolve the three-body problem by ejecting one star.

shots.narration: Three equal stars enter a mutual gravitational dance. Because three bodies cannot share energy evenly, their paths become chaotic almost immediately.
With every close pass, momentum transfers unevenly between them. Two bodies briefly pair up, while the third drains energy from their center of mass.
Eventually, a single tight encounter imparts enough kinetic energy to fling one star outward forever, leaving the remaining pair in a stable binary orbit.
